label: Statutory tuition fee (government-set)
notes: The statutory fee applies mainly to EU/EEA students and some others who meet nationality and prior-study conditions. Most non-EEA students pay the higher institutional fee instead. Re-verified against the source on 22 November 2026.

label: Institutional tuition fee (non-EEA)
notes: Non-EEA students pay an institutional fee set by each university. For 2026-2027 the source states bachelor's programmes average €9,000-20,000 and master's programmes €12,000-30,000; technical and medical programmes sit at the top. Exact figures per programme are on each institution's own page.

label: Application / handling fee (some institutions)
notes: Some institutions charge non-EEA applicants a handling fee of roughly €75-100 when they submit an application. This is a university charge, not an agency fee.

label: Living costs
notes: Covers rent, food, transport, insurance and personal expenses. Amsterdam and Utrecht sit at the higher end; smaller cities are cheaper. Budget for the higher end to be safe.

provenance.source: Study in NL - Costs of living

label: Proof of funds required for the visa
notes: For the entry visa/residence permit, non-EU students must prove roughly €1,130 per month for 12 months (about €13,569), on top of any unpaid tuition. This money must be shown as available; it is not a fee paid to anyone.

provenance.source: Dutch immigration service (IND) - income requirements for study

label: Residence permit / entry visa fee
notes: A non-refundable government fee for the residence permit, usually paid to and handled by your university as your sponsor. This is a government charge, not an agency service fee.

label: Health insurance
notes: International students need valid health insurance. A student policy can be relatively cheap; if you work alongside study you may be required to switch to Dutch public insurance, which costs more.

provenance.source: Study in NL - Plan your stay (insurance)
